subject: physics
question_text: Can a room be cooled by leaving the door of an electric refrigerator open?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 12 Very Short Answer Question 18 (printed p.126). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: a refrigerator rejects the heat it removes from its interior plus the work its compressor does, Q₁ = Q₂ + W; with the door open the room is both the cold space losing heat and the surroundings receiving Q₁, so the net effect is a small rise in room temperature, not a fall.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: How a refrigerator works
lines: No. A refrigerator removes heat from its
cold interior and rejects that heat, plus
the work done by its compressor, into the
steps.margin_note: First mark. Say a refrigerator rejects the heat removed plus the compressor's work.
steps.why: Over a cycle the first law gives Q_rejected = Q_removed + W, so the heat dumped into the room always exceeds the heat taken out of the cold space by the compressor's work.
common_mistakes: Saying a refrigerator only moves heat, with nothing added. The compressor does work, and that work is rejected as heat too.
Answering yes. The room cannot be cooled at all, because the refrigerator adds the compressor's work to the room as heat.

recall.must_convey: That a refrigerator removes heat from its cold interior and rejects that heat plus the compressor's work into the room.
accept: rejects heat plus the work done
reject: the room is both the cold space and the surroundings

steps.memory_tip: A refrigerator rejects more heat than it removes — the extra is the compressor's work.

steps.label: With the door open
lines: With the door open, the room is both the
cold space AND the surroundings that get
the rejected heat. More heat re-enters the
room than left it, so the room grows
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Say the room is both the cold space and the surroundings, so it ends up slightly warmer.
steps.why: The extra heat is the compressor's own work turned to heat, and with the door open it can only flow back into the same room.
common_mistakes: Saying the room stays the same temperature. The compressor keeps adding its own work as heat, so the room actually warms.
Treating the room as only the cold space. With the door open it is also the surroundings the heat is rejected into.

recall.must_convey: That with the door open the room is both the cold space and the surroundings, so more heat enters it than leaves, and the room grows slightly warmer.
accept: room is both the cold space and the surroundings
more heat comes back than left

steps.memory_tip: The compressor's own work has to go back into the same room when the door is open.

insider_note: The answer is no, and the full reason is the compressor's added work, not simply that heat moves — both parts belong in the answer.
